architecture.mechanism: Carbon-based microwave susceptors absorb microwave energy and convert it into localized thermal energy, with uptake governed by the susceptor's surface area and porosity, enabling targeted heating at lower bulk power.
architecture.intervention: Install a food-safe, high-surface-area carbon-loaded susceptor plate/sleeve inside the countertop cavity, positioned beneath and around the food, so it preferentially captures microwave energy from the standing-wave field and re-emits it as evenly distributed conductive/radiant heat into the food center, flattening the hot-edge/cold-center gradient with no user stirring.
architecture.expected_effect: Markedly lower spatial temperature non-uniformity across the load (edges no longer burn while the center stays cold), achieved passively within the existing countertop form factor and a standard single cycle.
architecture.falsification_test: Heat a fixed reference load (e.g., 200 g starch gel in a shallow Petri dish) at rated power for 60 s with and without the susceptor plate; map surface temperature by IR thermography and center temperature by fiber-optic probe, then compute max−min ΔT and spatial standard deviation; the mechanism is falsified if ΔT is not reduced by at least 30% or if edge temperature still exceeds center temperature by more than 10 °C.
